chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever plants a tree or digs a barren valley that no one has preceded him to, or revives dead land, it is his by decree of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger.'

key_terms.لم يسبقه إليه أحد: No one preceded him to it

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on owning land that one revives or plants trees in?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the principle of *iqya'* (reviving dead land), establishing that ownership is acquired through labor and exclusive cultivation of unclaimed land. It reflects the Prophetic tradition where the right to land is contingent upon active utilization, a concept deeply integrated into Shia fiqh regarding property rights and agricultural inheritance. The narration underscores the divine sanction of private ownership derived from personal effort in transforming barren land into productive assets.
